title: Take a terminal block from a person's hand, then snap it onto a loose DIN rail
instruction: Take the terminal block from the person's hand: grip it while they still hold it, so they can let go. Then press it straight down onto the DIN rail until it clicks, without knocking the rail out of place.
context: A person passing parts to a robot at a bench is routine in assembly cells; the robot has to receive them gently (no snatching, no pressing on the hand) before it can use them.
setup: On the table in front of the arms: a loose steel TS35 x 7.5 top-hat DIN rail, 240 mm long, 150 g, lying open side up and running left to right, its centre 0.30 m in front of the arm bases and 0.04 m right of their midline; fixed on it, a zinc end bracket near each end and a beige terminal block mounted against the left bracket. A person's hand and forearm (skin-coloured, grey sleeve, 30 cm forearm) reach in over the far edge of the table, holding a blue polyamide terminal block (a screw-clamp feed-through block: 5.1 mm thick, 60 mm long, 46 mm tall, about 8 g, a spring foot at each end of its base) pinched between thumb and index finger by its far end, low down, upright, its length pointing at the robot. Over 3 s the hand brings it to 0.36 m in front of the arms, 0.15 m right of their midline and 13 cm above the table, and holds it there, drifting by up to 3 mm. It lets go only after both fingertips of a robot gripper have pressed the block with 2 N or more for 0.3 s, then withdraws; otherwise it keeps holding the block out.
scoring: At the end of the run: 1.0 if the block was handed over cleanly and is latched on the rail (both feet clicked under the lips: seated within 0.8 mm, centred within 1 mm, square and level within 3 degrees, between the right bracket and the beige block), released (the gripper not touching it) and still for 1 s; 0.75 latched; 0.5 resting on the rail (within 4 mm of centre, base within 8 mm of the lips, tilt under 10 degrees); 0.25 handed over cleanly (the hand let go into the robot's grip); else 0. Score 0 if, at any moment, the load on the hand exceeded 5 N (the net force on the hand and forearm from the robot and the block, read by a force sensor between the prop hand and its stand: pushing or pulling the block against the hand counts), the robot pressed on the hand or forearm with more than 10 N in total, or the block left the hand before it let go (snatched). Capped at 0.25 if the block was dropped or the rail moved 10 mm or turned 3 degrees.
reset_notes: Put the block back in the prop's pinch, zero its force sensor, and put the rail back in place; a latched block cannot be pulled straight off: spread a foot with a screwdriver to remove it. The prop is a rigid hand and forearm on a sprung slide (about 1.5 N/mm) through a 6-axis force/torque sensor, with pressure-sensing film on its pads and forearm; an operator opens its sprung thumb once both robot fingertips have closed on the block.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. The hand is rigid boxes on sprung slides (gives 1.5 N/mm, pinches 2.8 N) with a fixed script that reacts only to the robot's grip; the load on the hand and the robot's contact with it are read after every physics step. The block is a generic screw-clamp design with a spring stand-in for the latch (clicks at ~5 N, likely below a real block); rail lips 2 mm (1 mm real). Block velocity from pose change.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; the arms never reached for the block); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 435, the block latched and released). Checks in the README: push (block shoved into the hand, 7.5 N load) 0; snatch 0; rough 0; no-press 0.5; drop 0.25.
